content.text: you can certainly create complex expressions via plugin.
Here is an example of Javascript expression evaluator:
But you should not think about it as two separate tags combining value, eg [[fixed1:something]:with([[fixed2:something else]])] but rather as a single tag with more complex expression
[[fixed:custom expression(do this and that with field 1 and field 2)]]
A good practice to do in such case is to pass root object for processing for easier access to entirety of the model.
Meaning instead of doing something like
pass it together via a root object, eg
templater.process( new { col1 = collection1, col2 = collection2 })
> we are currently trying to figure out, whether we can sum 2 variables
> In an example we saw it is possible to sum the elements of a structure
> Is it possible to do it for 2 separate lists and then sum the results?
> Also, is it possible to sum 2 different variables together?
Hello , we add new functionality for this task , !Sum and !SumAdd , examples for both of cases in template file.
If you have any questions, write to me and I will try to help you.
Looks great! I will test and let you know.
I just tested with more than one POD in the DD and I expected this expression
To sum on POD level, meaning that we will have an array of sums as a result - one for DD!at(0), one for DD!at(1) and so on. Instead we get a total sum over all PODs. Can this behavior be chaged?
can you show me your template file and invoice?
Do you want to sum the variables ‘TablePCProfiles.Value’ and ‘TablePCScales.ListPC.Value’ separately?
Or do you want to sum the variables for each POD separately?
I want to sum TablePCProfiles.Value for 1 POD with the TablePCScales.ListPC.Value for the same POD
Do you want to add a general logic so that “Sum” and “SumAdd” always sum the variables single POD only?
And how should we determine exactly which POD variables need to be summed?
or we should sum variables for all POD, but display total amount of variables for each POD separately?
